# To-do list

The screen of the one shared to-do list. Anybody who opens it adds a task of one line, ticks it
done and back, corrects its text and deletes it, and reads the same list, newest first, as
everybody else — with no sign-in, because there is no identity here
([`../../contexts/todo_list.md`](../../contexts/todo_list.md) § `P-02`).

The screen renders inside the page frame ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md)). The frame owns
the lockup, the navigation between the screens, the layout of the header and the not-found page;
this document owns what the to-do list puts into that frame. The mock-up in the front matter was
drafted by the process and approved as drafted by the person who asked for the change; it holds
the pixels, and this document is the specification ([`README.md`](README.md)).

A requirement written `R-n` below is `CR-2609-823a/R-n`.

## Regions

Top to bottom, inside the page frame:

1. **Header** — the frame's lockup and navigation, with "To-do list" marked as the screen on
   show, and on the right the number of tasks (R-5, R-3).
2. **Title and introductory sentence** — "Things to do", and one sentence on what the list is
   for and what using it costs (R-1).
3. **The add field** — one line and "Add task", in a white card (R-1, R-2).
4. **The list** — directly under the add field: every task, newest first, done and not done
   alike. In its place while it loads, rows in outline; when there is no task, the empty
   sentence; when it could not be read, the failure sentence and the error card (R-3, R-4,
   R-10).
5. **Footer** — one sentence about who sees this.
6. **The delete question** — above the screen, only while a deletion is being asked (R-7).
7. **Notices** — the frame's toasts, bottom right: what went through, and what did not (R-8,
   R-10).

## Components and their states

### The task count in the header

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| default | `6 tasks`, `1 task` — how many tasks the list holds, as last read |
| empty | `0 tasks` |
| loading | no number at all: none is shown before the list has been read |
| error | no number at all: a list that could not be read has no count |

States omitted: hover, focus, active, disabled — it is a fact in text, not a control.

### The add field (R-1, R-2)

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| default | a white card holding one borderless field, with the placeholder "What needs doing?", and "Add task" on its right. The field has no visible label and is named "New task" for assistive technology. It takes every character typed or pasted: nothing stops input at a length, and there is no character counter |
| focus | the screen's focus ring on the field; nothing moves |
| hover | "Add task", while it is open, lightens slightly; the field does not change |
| disabled | "Add task" is closed while the field holds no text, or holds a text the screen's rule refuses. Why: once the field has been left or Enter pressed, the rule's sentence stands under the field (`error`); before that, the empty field and its placeholder say what it is waiting for. Field and button are both locked while an add travels, and "Adding…" says why (`loading`) |
| error | the sentence for the one reason the text is refused, under the field, in the danger colour, announced as an alert, with the field marked invalid. Nothing is sent and the list does not change. It appears after the field is left or on Enter, never while typing, and goes as soon as the text passes |
| loading | "Adding…" on the button; the field and the button locked, the typed text still in the field; no row appears until the answer |

States omitted: active — no pressed look of its own: a press shows as the state it starts,
`loading` or `error`; empty — the field's emptiness is its `default` state, and the empty list
is the list's own state, below.

**The screen's rule is the service's rule, applied before sending** (`BR-06`, `BR-07`). The text
is normalized and trimmed exactly as the service will do it, then judged, in this order: empty,
then more than one line, then longer than 200 code points — so a text that is both too long and
more than one line gets the one-line sentence. The screen accepts exactly the texts the service
accepts: two hundred emoji are taken whole and "Add task" opens, two hundred and one are refused
as too long. A line feed or a carriage return never reaches the field, because a one-line field
drops them; the other five line breaks can be pasted, often invisibly, and are refused with the
one-line sentence.

### The list (R-3, R-4, R-10)

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| loading | four rows in outline inside the list's card, with the height reserved and no spinner; read aloud as "Loading tasks". The add field is usable meanwhile |
| empty | "No tasks yet. Add the first one above." in a dashed frame where the list would be. Nothing reads as an error, and the header says `0 tasks` |
| default | every stored task in one white card, one row per task, the rows parted by hairlines, newest first, done and not done alike. Nothing to press to see more, however many tasks there are: the footer follows the last task. A list whose every task is done is this state, not `empty` |
| error | "The tasks could not be loaded." above the shared error card ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Components and their states), whose title says what went wrong — "Could not reach the service" when nothing answered — with the detail it was given and "Try again". The empty sentence is not shown, the header shows no count, and the add field stays usable |

States omitted: hover, focus, active, disabled — the list is not a control; the controls are in
its rows, below.

**The list shows the tasks in the order they arrive and sorts nothing** (`BR-11`). A tick and a
correction never move a task.

### A task's row (R-4, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10)

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| default | an empty box, the task's text beside it, and the quiet text buttons "Edit" and "Delete" on the right, always visible. The text is the box's label, so pressing the text ticks the box too. A long text wraps inside the row, and an unbroken run breaks anywhere rather than widening the page |
| done | the box filled with the accent colour and ticked; the text struck through in the muted text colour and exactly as readable as any other text; the row stays where it was |
| hover | over the box and its text the pointer says they can be pressed; "Edit" turns the accent colour and "Delete" the danger colour; a locked control does not change |
| focus | the screen's focus ring around the box (the checkbox itself is not drawn), and around "Edit" and "Delete" |
| loading | a tick travelling: the box locked and still showing the state that is stored, with "Saving…" beside it. The row's "Edit" and "Delete" and every other row stay usable |
| editing | the text replaced, in place, by a bordered field holding the stored text, with the focus in it, and "Save" and "Cancel" under it; "Edit" reads "Editing". The box stays usable; "Delete" stays usable. At most one row is ever editing, and the list does not move |
| saving | "Saving…" on "Save"; the edit field, "Save" and "Cancel" locked; "Edit" locked on every row until the answer |
| deleting | behind the open question: "Deleting…" in place of "Delete", and "Edit" locked |
| disabled | "Edit" is closed on the row being edited, where it reads "Editing" because the editor is already open, and on every row while a correction travels, where the "Saving…" on the row being saved says why. "Delete" is closed only while its own deletion travels, and reads "Deleting…". The box is closed only while its own tick travels, with "Saving…" beside it |
| error | a correction the screen's rule refuses: the sentence under the edit field, announced as an alert, the field marked invalid, and "Save" closed until the text passes; "Cancel" brings back the stored text. A change that did not go through leaves the row showing what is stored — the box as it was, the text as it was — and a notice says why; a correction that did not go through keeps the editor open with what was typed, so it can be sent again or cancelled |

States omitted: active — no pressed look of its own: a press shows as the state it starts;
empty — a row exists only for a stored task, and a stored task always has text (`BR-06`).

**A task shows done in three ways at once** — the tick, the strike-through and the checked state
assistive technology reads — so colour is never the only carrier (`BR-09`). The done text is
`--color-muted`, which measures 7.09:1 on the card; it is never greyed with `--color-disabled` or
with opacity, which is the defect recorded in [`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens.

**Editing happens in the row, one row at a time, and the words stay where they were read** —
the guestbook card's editing ([`guestbook.md`](guestbook.md) § The entry card), with the same
lock: while a correction travels, no editor opens anywhere, so the answer can only close the
editor that sent it. Opening "Edit" on another row closes the open editor, and what was typed
there is dropped. Ticking the box of a row being edited leaves the editor open with what was
typed. Escape does nothing in the editor: a stray key must not lose an edit. A done task is
corrected exactly as a not-done one, and its box stays ticked throughout (`BR-10`).

### The delete question (R-7, R-8)

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| default | over the dimmed screen: "Delete this task?", the task's text quoted, "This cannot be undone.", then "Cancel", which has the focus, and "Delete task". The task is still on the list behind it |
| hover | "Cancel" takes the medium surface and ink text; "Delete task" lightens slightly |
| focus | the focus ring; the focus starts on "Cancel", and Tab stays inside the question in both directions |
| active | the shared buttons' own pressed look: each shrinks slightly while pressed |
| loading | "Deleting…" on "Delete task"; both buttons locked; Escape and a press on the backdrop do nothing; the focus rests on the question itself |
| disabled | both buttons, only while a deletion travels, and "Deleting…" says why |

States omitted: empty — the question opens only for a task on the list, and quotes it; error — a
deletion that did not go through closes the question and is told by a notice (§ Interactions).

**The question quotes the task it is about**, and the focus starts on "Cancel", so an Enter
pressed out of habit deletes nothing — the guestbook's delete dialog, and its focus rules, as
they are ([`guestbook.md`](guestbook.md) § The delete dialog).

### Notices (R-8, R-10)

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| success | a dark notice at the bottom right, with a tick: "Task added.", "Task updated." or "Task deleted."; it goes by itself after a few seconds. A tick gets no notice: the box is its own confirmation |
| error | a dark notice with the error glyph, saying what was not done (§ Copy); it stays until it is dismissed with its "×". The screen under it is unchanged, so the lasting fact is on the screen and not only in the notice |
| hover | the "×" brightens |
| focus | the focus ring around the "×" |

States omitted: active, disabled, loading, empty — a notice exists only while it has something
to say, carries nothing to wait for, and its one button is always usable and has no pressed look
of its own.

## Copy

English, like the rest of this repository ([`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Language).

| Key | Copy |
|---|---|
| screen title | `Things to do` |
| introductory sentence | `No account, no sign-in, one list for everybody. Add what needs doing and tick it off when it is done. Anyone can edit or delete any task.` |
| task count | `0 tasks` · `1 task` · `6 tasks` |
| add field placeholder | `What needs doing?` |
| add button | `Add task` |
| add button in flight | `Adding…` |
| empty list | `No tasks yet. Add the first one above.` |
| list failed to load | `The tasks could not be loaded.` — above the shared error card, whose copy is [`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Copy |
| row actions | `Edit` · `Delete` |
| row being edited | `Editing` |
| editor | `Save` · `Saving…` · `Cancel` |
| tick in flight | `Saving…` |
| deletion in flight | `Deleting…` — on the row and on the question |
| question — title | `Delete this task?` |
| question — quotation | the task's text, as stored |
| question — consequence | `This cannot be undone.` |
| question — buttons | `Cancel` · `Delete task` · `Deleting…` |
| notice after adding | `Task added.` |
| notice after correcting | `Task updated.` |
| notice after deleting | `Task deleted.` |
| an add not stored, nothing answered | `The task was not added: the service could not be reached.` |
| a tick, correction or deletion not stored, nothing answered | `The change was not made: the service could not be reached.` |
| a change not stored, the service answered with an error of no sentence of its own | not decided — § States with no defined behaviour, question 1 |
| footer | `Tasks are public and editable by anyone with this link.` |

The sentence says "the service could not be reached" only when no answer came at all.

### The refusals this screen can show

The words live beside the endpoint that produces them, in
[`../api.md`](../api.md) § The to-do list's refusals, and this screen shows them as they are
written there, from the refusal's `message`:

| Code | Where it is shown |
|---|---|
| `todo_task_text_empty` | under the add field or the edit field |
| `todo_task_text_multiline` | under the add field or the edit field |
| `todo_task_text_too_long` | under the add field or the edit field |
| `todo_task_not_found` | in an error notice, after a tick, a correction or a deletion; nothing else on the screen changes |

**The screen's own verdict before sending uses the same three text sentences, word for word**, so
one text is refused on the screen and by the service for the same reason in the same words
(`BR-06`). If the service refuses a text the screen let through, its sentence stands in the same
place under the field and the text stays as typed.

Never shown, because this screen never provokes them: `todo_task_empty_patch` (every change it
sends carries a text or a done mark) and the standard validation refusal (it never sends a
malformed request).

### Accessibility labels

Text nobody sees and assistive technology reads. Here for the same reason as the rest: a test
and the smoke find elements by it.

| Text | Where |
|---|---|
| `New task` | the add field |
| `Edit task` | the edit field |
| `Tasks` | the list |
| `Loading tasks` | the list while it loads, a status region |
| the task's text | each box: the visible text is its label; while the row is editing, the stored text names it |
| `Edit “<text>”` · `Delete “<text>”` | each row's buttons: the visible word followed by that task's text in quotation marks |
| `Dismiss notification` | the "×" on a notice (the shared toast) |

## Data

Bound to the live contract, [`../api.md`](../api.md). One hook reads and writes the resource; no
screen element calls the client itself.

| Element | Source | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| the task count | `GET /api/todo-tasks` through `useTodoTasks()` | `total` |
| the rows, in the order they arrive | `GET /api/todo-tasks` through `useTodoTasks()` | `items[].id`, `items[].text`, `items[].done` |
| the empty state | `GET /api/todo-tasks` through `useTodoTasks()` | `items` empty, `total` 0 |
| adding | `POST /api/todo-tasks` through the add mutation of `useTodoTasks.ts` | sends `text` as typed; answered by one `TodoTaskRead` |
| ticking | `PATCH /api/todo-tasks/{todo_task_id}` through its mark mutation | sends `done` alone — `true` or `false`, the state the person chose; `todo_task_id` is the row's `id` |
| correcting | `PATCH /api/todo-tasks/{todo_task_id}` through its correction mutation | sends `text` alone |
| deleting | `DELETE /api/todo-tasks/{todo_task_id}` through its delete mutation | sends nothing; answered `204` |
| the sentence of a refusal | the body of any refused write above | `detail.code` decides where it is shown, `detail.message` is the words |

**A tick sends the state chosen, never "the opposite of what is stored"**, and it sends `done`
alone; a correction sends `text` alone. That is the screen's half of `BR-09` and `BR-10`: two
people ticking the same task done both end with it done, and a tick and a correction sent at the
same moment are both kept.

**A change is shown as made only once the answer says it was stored** — no row, tick or text
appears ahead of the answer — and the list is read again after every change that went through,
which is also when other people's changes arrive
([`../architecture.md`](../architecture.md) § The to-do list — where each rule lives).
`created_at` is not shown: it orders the list, and the order is the answer's.

## Interactions

- **Typing in the add field** → nothing is judged while typing; "Add task" opens the moment the
  screen's rule accepts the text.
- **Leaving the add field, or Enter, with no text or a refused text** → the rule's sentence under
  the field; nothing is sent.
- **"Add task", or Enter, with an accepted text** → the task is sent; meanwhile "Adding…", the
  field and the button locked, no row. On success the task appears first in the list with the
  frame's one entry animation, the count follows, the field is emptied and a notice says
  "Task added.". If nothing answered: the notice "The task was not added: the service could not
  be reached.", no row, and the text stays in the field for a retry. If the service refused the
  text: its sentence under the field, and the text stays.
- **Pressing the box or its text, or Space on the box** → the chosen state is sent; meanwhile the
  box is locked on the stored state with "Saving…" beside it. On success the box and the text
  show the stored state and the row stays in its place; no notice. If the task no longer exists:
  the `todo_task_not_found` sentence in a notice, the box as it was, and the row stays until the
  list is read again. If nothing answered: "The change was not made: the service could not be
  reached.", and the box as it was.
- **"Edit"** → the row's editor opens with this task's stored text and the focus in the field;
  an editor open on another row closes.
- **"Edit" while a correction travels** → nothing: it is locked on every row until the answer.
- **Leaving the edit field, or Enter, with a refused text** → the rule's sentence under the field;
  nothing is sent.
- **"Save", or Enter in the edit field, with an accepted text** → the text is sent; meanwhile the
  `saving` state. On success the editor closes, the new text stands in the task's place, its done
  state as it was, and a notice says "Task updated.". If the task no longer exists: the
  `todo_task_not_found` sentence in a notice; the editor stays open with what was typed and no
  task with the new text appears. If nothing answered: "The change was not made: the service
  could not be reached.", and the editor stays open with what was typed. In both, the stored text
  is unchanged and comes back on "Cancel". If the service refused the text: its sentence under
  the edit field.
- **"Cancel" in the editor** → the editor closes and the stored text shows; nothing is sent.
- **"Delete"** → the question opens over the screen; nothing is sent.
- **"Cancel", Escape, or a press on the backdrop** → the question closes and the task is as it
  was.
- **"Delete task"** → the deletion is sent; meanwhile the question's `loading` state and the row's
  `deleting` state. On success the question closes, the row goes, every other row is untouched,
  and a notice says "Task deleted."; there is no undo anywhere. Deleting the last task brings back
  the empty sentence. If the task no longer exists: the question closes and the
  `todo_task_not_found` sentence stands in a notice; the row stays until the list is read again.
  If nothing answered: the question closes, "The change was not made: the service could not be
  reached.", and the row stays. A deletion of the row being edited closes its editor with it.
- **"Try again" on a list that could not be read** → the list is read again; the error card stays
  until the answer, then the list, the empty sentence or the card again.
- **"×" on a notice** → the notice goes.
- **Opening the to-do list's own address, or reloading it** → the list is read and shown as it is
  stored at that moment, including what other people added, ticked, corrected or deleted. Nothing
  pushes their changes to an open screen.
- **The navigation, the lockup and the main address** → the frame's
  ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Interactions).

Keyboard: every action above works without a mouse — see the next section.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- **The Tab order** is the frame's lockup and navigation, the add field, "Add task" when it is
  open, then row by row from the top: the box, "Edit", "Delete"; in a row being edited, the box,
  the edit field, "Save", "Cancel", "Delete". A locked control is skipped.
- **Enter in the add field** adds an accepted text or shows the rule's sentence. **Space on a
  box** ticks it or unticks it. **Enter in the edit field** saves an accepted text or shows the
  sentence. **Escape** does nothing in the editor and closes the question, except while a
  deletion travels.
- **After a successful add the focus stays in the add field**, so the next task can be typed at
  once. **The question takes the focus on "Cancel"**, keeps Tab inside itself, and on closing
  hands the focus back to the "Delete" that opened it — or, when that row is gone, to the list,
  never to the page's start. Where the focus goes in the other moments a control it was on is
  locked or removed is not decided: § States with no defined behaviour, question 2.
- **The focus ring is the screen's**, in the accent colour, on everything that can take the focus:
  the add field, each box (drawn around the box), "Edit", "Delete", the edit field, "Save",
  "Cancel", the question's buttons and a notice's "×". No component removes it
  ([`guestbook.md`](guestbook.md) § The composer card).
- **Refusal sentences are announced** as alerts and the field they belong to is marked invalid.
  Success notices are announced politely and error notices at once, by the shared toast.
- **Contrast.** Every text clears 4.5:1 on the surface behind it: the task text in ink, the done
  text in `--color-muted` (7.09:1 on the card), the placeholder, "Edit", "Delete" and "Saving…"
  in `--color-faint` (5.40:1 on the card). An unticked box's edge is `--color-faint` too, which
  clears the 3:1 a control's edge needs to be seen; `--color-line` would not. A locked control's
  text is exempt, as `--color-disabled` is ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens).
- **Reduced motion.** The entry animation of a new row is not played when the person asks for
  reduced motion.

## Tokens

Colour and typeface from `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`, and nothing else. Spacing, sizes and
radii outside the named ones come from Tailwind's own scale — never a bracketed value and never a
raw hex.

| Use | Token |
|---|---|
| the add field's card, the list's card, a row's box when unticked, the edit field, the question | `--color-card` |
| the edges of those cards, the rows' separators, the edit field's edge, "Cancel"'s edge | `--color-hairline` |
| the dashed frame of the empty list | `--color-line` |
| the task text, the typed text | `--color-ink` |
| done text, struck through; the empty sentence; the failure sentence; "Cancel"'s text | `--color-muted` |
| the placeholder; "Edit", "Delete" and "Saving…"; an unticked box's edge | `--color-faint` |
| "Add task", "Save"; a ticked box's fill and edge; "Edit" on hover; the focus ring | `--color-accent` |
| the text on "Add task" and "Save"; the tick | `--color-inverse` |
| a refusal sentence under a field; "Delete" on hover | `--color-danger` |
| "Cancel" on hover; the outline rows while loading | `--color-surface-medium` |
| the quotation in the question; a locked edit field | `--color-surface` |
| the cards | `--radius-card` |
| "Add task" | `--radius-control` |
| the edit field, "Save", "Cancel" | `--radius-control-tight` |
| the question | `--radius-modal` |
| "Edit", "Delete", "Saving…", "Save", "Cancel", the failure sentence | `--text-meta` |
| the empty sentence | `--text-body` |
| the title | `--font-serif`; everything else `--font-sans` |
| a new row arriving | `--animate-rise` |
| a closed "Add task" or "Save" | the scale's `opacity-35`, as on the guestbook; a locked box or row button `opacity-50` |
| "Add task" and "Save" on hover | the scale's `brightness-112`, as the guestbook's post button |

The frame's own tokens — the column's width, the header, the footer, the navigation — are
[`system-states.md`](system-states.md)'s, and the notices, the question's backdrop and the error
card are the shared primitives', unchanged by this screen.

## States with no defined behaviour

Two questions the mock-up and the requirements leave open. Neither is filled in here; each waits
for a person's answer.

1. **The words of a failed change when the service answered with an error of no sentence of its
   own** — a server error, for instance, rather than a coded refusal or no answer at all. The
   mock-up words the two cases it drew: nothing answered ("…the service could not be reached.")
   and a refusal with a sentence ("that sentence"). "Could not be reached" is untrue when the
   service did answer.
2. **Where the focus goes when a control it was on is locked for a write and then unlocked, or
   removed**: the box after a tick settles, the add field after an add fails, the edit field after
   a correction fails, and the row after its editor closes on "Save" or "Cancel". Neither the
   mock-up nor the guestbook it follows says; the guestbook today leaves it to the browser, which
   can drop the focus to the start of the page.

## Out of scope for this screen

- **Anything to do with identity.** No sign-in, no "my tasks", no record of who added, ticked or
  corrected a task.
- **Showing the moment of adding.** It orders the list and is not shown.
- **Search, filters, pages, "clear all done", reordering, due dates, owners.** The context's
  non-goals ([`../../contexts/todo_list.md`](../../contexts/todo_list.md) § Deliberate non-goals).
- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is read again.
- **Telling somebody their change was replaced.** The later change wins, silently (`BR-10`).
- **Undo and restore.** A deleted task is gone (`BR-13`).
- **A special state for "every task done".** Such a list is simply a list of done tasks.
- **A character counter.** The field takes every character, and the sentence under it is the
  bound.
- **Other window shapes.** This stack declares no window classes, so the screen is one layout: the
  column narrows with the window, and a phone layout is a named non-goal
  ([`../../invariants.md`](../../invariants.md) § Deliberate non-goals).
- **Other languages and a dark theme.** English only; one palette
  ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § One palette).

# Screens

One document per screen, saying what that screen is: regions, components with the full set of
their states, the copy, the data bindings to the API contract, the interactions and the tokens
used. Template: `.specconf/templates/system/ui-screen.md`.

## HTML is the evidence, Markdown is the truth

A change touching a screen delivers a Claude Design mock-up as
`spec/changes/<CR>/design/ui/index.html` and derives the screen document from it.

The mock-up is kept, in the change's directory, as a record of what was agreed. It is not the
specification and cannot be, for three reasons, all of them mechanical rather than stylistic:

- **It cannot be diffed.** Changing one word of copy and completely relaying the layout produce
  the same unreadable diff, so no reviewer can tell them apart.
- **It cannot be merged.** Two changes touching the same screen produce a conflict nobody will
  resolve by reading it.
- **A requirement cannot be cited in it.** A screenshot has nowhere to put
  `@req:CR-2608-a7f3/R-6`, and traceability that stops at the browser stops.

So the Markdown carries the requirement references, the states, the copy and the bindings; the
HTML carries the pixels. An implementer builds from the Markdown and may open the HTML for
orientation.

## Why states are enumerated

Every component lists **only the states that exist on the built screen** (`default`, `empty`,
`error`, `loading`, `disabled`, … — the names keep their source form, because they are
identifiers matching CSS and component states). A row whose content would be "not implemented"
says nothing a reader can use. It also lists the ones the mock-up does not draw, where they
exist in the code: a mock-up draws the happy path, and the `empty` state is the one a
back-office screen actually lives in on its first day. States considered and genuinely absent
are declared in a "States omitted" line under the table — the template says how.

A state not listed is not an oversight for an implementer to fill in quietly; it is a question
for that change's requirements stage.

## Why the copy is here

Labels, hints, empty-state sentences and messages are **product content** rather than an
implementation detail — English, like the rest of this repository
([`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Language). They are agreed with the person who will
read them, they are reviewed, and they belong in a document a non-programmer can open.

The refusal sentences an operator sees are the exception that proves the rule: they live beside
the endpoint that produces them (see [`../api.md`](../api.md)), and a screen document says which
of them that screen can display.

## Naming

`<screen-slug>.md`, matching the route, with front matter carrying `route`, `info_ref` (the
frozen screen identifier `S-xx`, if one exists) and the requirements the screen satisfies.

1	# Requirements — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done
2	
3	**Change:** CR-2609-823a
4	**Source:** request.md, impact.md, brainstorm.md (answers `Q-1`…`Q-9`), and the answers
5	`Q-10`…`Q-12` recorded in the change record on 2026-09-24
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	Anybody who opens the application can reach a second screen, a shared to-do list, add a task
10	of one line, tick it done and back, correct it and delete it, while the guestbook stays where
11	it is and keeps working as it does today.
12	
13	Words used below, none of which is in `spec/glossary.md` yet (giving them a home is the design
14	stage's job): a **task** is one line of text somebody put on the list; **the to-do list** is the
15	one list of tasks every visitor shares; **done** and **not done** are the one state a task has,
16	switched both ways; **the moment of adding** is when the system stored a task. It orders the
17	list and never changes.
18	
19	## Success criteria
20	
21	| Id | Criterion | Baseline | How measured after delivery |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **SC-1** | A person who has never seen the to-do list reaches it from the guestbook, adds a task and finds it at the top of the list, with no instruction. | None. Nobody can add a task today: no to-do concept exists in the specification or in the code (`impact.md` § What is missing). | The requester follows the `uat.md` script on the delivered branch before merging and records pass or fail per step. That is the one look after delivery this template schedules. |
24	| **SC-2** | Two people looking at the list after a reload see the same tasks, in the same order, with the same done marks. | None. The guestbook is the only thing people share today, and it has no state anybody marks. | The requester checks it at UAT with two browser windows (`uat.md`). The scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-3` and `CR-2609-823a/R-9` re-check it on every CI run of the branch. |
25	| **SC-3** | A task ticked done by mistake goes back to not done in one action, and neither action moves it in the list. | None. Nothing the application stores has a state that can be switched (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`: "An entry either exists or it does not"). | A `uat.md` step at UAT, plus the scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-4` on every CI run. |
26	| **SC-4** | A reviewer who opens a freshly created environment sees example tasks on the list without typing any. | A freshly created environment opens today with the guestbook's welcome entries (`golden-set/seed/entries-welcome.json`) and nothing else. | The reviewer opens the first preview of this branch (Actions → Preview), or runs `./scripts/start.sh` on a fresh clone, and counts the example tasks. This is manual because the black box starts with `--no-seed` (`R-11`). |
27	| **SC-5** | A guest who knows the guestbook finds it where it was: the main address still opens it and everything it did before still works. | The main address redirects to the guestbook (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Interactions). The 22 scenarios in `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` pass. | The 22 scenarios of `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` run unchanged on every CI run of this branch. The UI smoke's guestbook tests keep asserting what they assert today; a locator that names the lockup or a navigation link may follow the names the user approves in the mock-up (§ Open questions; Self-check 14; assumed: `A-4`, § Named assumptions). The requester checks at UAT. |
28	
29	## Requirements
30	
31	### R-1: Adding a task — **P1**
32	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want to add a task by typing one line, so
33	that it joins the shared list of things to do.
34	**Why this priority:** Without it there is no list. Every other requirement acts on a task this
35	one creates.
36	**Independent test:** Add one task to an empty list and read the list back.
37	
38	1. The system SHALL present one screen holding one field for a new task's text, with the list of
39	   tasks below that field (`request.md`: "a simple view with a field for adding tasks and a list";
40	   `Q-6`: "right under the field").
41	2. The system SHALL let anybody who opens the to-do list add a task, with no account and no
42	   sign-in.
43	3. WHEN a person submits a text for a new task, the system SHALL store one task holding that
44	   text as `R-2` shapes it, record it as not done, and record its moment of adding.
45	4. WHEN a task has been added, the system SHALL show it first in the list without the person
46	   reloading the screen.
47	5. WHEN a person submits a text identical to the text of a task already on the list, the system
48	   SHALL store a second, separate task (`Q-9`).
49	
50	**Acceptance**
51	- **R-1.1** GIVEN an empty to-do list, WHEN a person adds the task "Water the plants", THEN the
52	  list holds exactly one task, its text is "Water the plants", and it is shown as not done.
53	- **R-1.2** GIVEN a list holding the task "Buy bread", WHEN a person adds "Buy bread" again,
54	  THEN the list holds two tasks with that text, and marking one of them done leaves the other
55	  not done.
56	- **R-1.3** GIVEN a list of two tasks, WHEN a person adds a third, THEN the third is shown first
57	  without the page being reloaded.
58	- **R-1.4** GIVEN a request to add a task that arrives already claiming to be done, WHEN it is
59	  stored, THEN the new task is not done.
60	
61	### R-2: What is not a task is refused — **P1**
62	**Objective:** As a reader of the list, I want empty and over-long texts kept out, so that the
63	list never shows a row with nothing in it.
64	**Why this priority:** It is the other half of `R-1`. Shipping `R-1` without it stores empty
65	rows on the first day.
66	**Independent test:** Submit a text of three spaces and confirm the list is unchanged.
67	
68	1. The system SHALL normalize a task's text to Unicode NFC and trim both of its ends of the
69	   written 30-code-point whitespace set, before it measures the text. This is the rule the
70	   system already applies to every text field it accepts (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend,
71	   on `app/platform/schemas/text.py`; the set is defined in `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`).
72	2. IF a task's text is empty after trimming, THEN the system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and
73	   tell the person that a task needs text.
74	3. IF a task's text is longer than 200 code points after normalizing and trimming, THEN the
75	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person that the text is too long.
76	4. WHERE a text, once clause 1 has trimmed it, still carries whitespace other than a line break,
77	   the system SHALL keep that whitespace unchanged.
78	5. The system SHALL accept on the screen exactly the texts the service accepts. The field
79	   SHALL NOT block, cut short or silently stop taking a text the service would store, and the
80	   screen SHALL NOT let through a text the service would refuse.
81	6. IF a task's text, once clause 1 has trimmed it, still carries a line break, THEN the
82	   system SHALL refuse it, store nothing, and tell the person, with a reason of its own, that a
83	   task is one line (`Q-11`: "Refuse it, with its own message"). A line break is any of U+000A,
84	   U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029: one written set that the screen and the
85	   service both read, never either language's default (assumed: `A-1`, § Named assumptions).
86	   Every one of them is in clause 1's trim set, so a line break at either end is removed by
87	   clause 1 and is not refused. A character that shows nothing but is not in the trim set, such
88	   as U+200B, is content, so a line break beside it is inside the text (assumed: `A-3`, § Named
89	   assumptions).
90	
91	**Acceptance**
92	- **R-2.1** GIVEN the text "   " (three spaces), WHEN it is submitted as a new task, THEN it is
93	  refused, the person is told why, and the list is unchanged. The same holds for the empty text.
94	- **R-2.2** GIVEN a text of exactly 200 code points, WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted
95	  and stored whole. GIVEN one of 201 code points, THEN it is refused and the list is unchanged.
96	- **R-2.3** GIVEN a text of 200 × U+1F600 (200 code points, 400 UTF-16 code units), WHEN it is
97	  typed or pasted into the field and submitted, THEN the screen takes every character and the
98	  service stores the task. GIVEN 201 of them, THEN the screen and the service both refuse it,
99	  for the same reason.
100	- **R-2.4** GIVEN a text of 200 letters, each written as U+0065 followed by U+0301 (400 code
101	  points before normalizing, 200 after), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as
102	  200 code points.
103	- **R-2.5** GIVEN a text of 200 code points with two spaces before it and two after (204 as
104	  typed), WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is accepted and stored as the 200 code points without
105	  the spaces. GIVEN a text of 205 spaces, THEN it is refused as empty, not as too long.
106	- **R-2.6** GIVEN the text "Buy  two   lamps", WHEN it is submitted, THEN it is stored with its
107	  inner spaces exactly as typed.
108	- **R-2.7** GIVEN the text "Buy bread", a line feed, then "and milk", WHEN it is submitted as a
109	  new task, THEN it is refused with the one-line reason, not as empty or too long, and the list
110	  is unchanged. GIVEN "Buy bread" followed by one line feed, THEN it is accepted and stored as
111	  "Buy bread".
112	
113	### R-3: One shared list, in one order — **P1**
114	**Objective:** As anybody who opens the to-do list, I want every task on one list in the order
115	the tasks were added, newest first, so that everybody reads the same list the same way.
116	**Why this priority:** The list is what a person looks at. Without a settled order two people
117	see two different lists, and a task just added gets lost among the others.
118	**Independent test:** Add three tasks, then read the list from a second browser.
119	
120	1. WHEN the to-do list is opened, the system SHALL show every stored task, done and not done
121	   alike, on one list, with no division into pages and no filter (`Q-9`).
122	2. The system SHALL order the list by moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`).
123	3. WHERE two tasks share a moment of adding, the system SHALL show them in the same relative
124	   order every time the list is read, so that the order is total.
125	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, or its text is edited, the system SHALL keep it in
126	   the same position in the list (`Q-4`, `Q-6`).
127	5. WHEN the list is opened or reloaded, the system SHALL show the tasks exactly as they are
128	   stored at that moment, including tasks other people have added, marked, edited or deleted.
129	6. WHEN the list holds no task, the system SHALL say that it is empty, with a sentence about what
130	   to do, and SHALL NOT present it as an error (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Components and their states:
131	   "Emptiness always carries a sentence about what to do").
132	
133	**Acceptance**
134	- **R-3.1** GIVEN the tasks "First", "Second" and "Third", added in that order, WHEN the list is
135	  opened, THEN it shows "Third", "Second", "First".
136	- **R-3.2** GIVEN two tasks with the same moment of adding, WHEN the list is read twice, THEN both
137	  reads show them in the same relative order.
138	- **R-3.3** GIVEN 101 stored tasks, WHEN the list is opened, THEN all 101 are shown on one list,
139	  with nothing to press to see more. (101 is one more than the largest piece the guestbook's read
140	  hands out, and more than its default piece of 20.)
141	- **R-3.4** GIVEN the list "Third", "Second", "First" with "Second" not done, WHEN "Second" is
142	  marked done, THEN the list still reads "Third", "Second", "First". The order is also unchanged
143	  after the text of "Second" is edited.
144	- **R-3.5** GIVEN person A has the list open, WHEN person B adds a task and A reloads the list,
145	  THEN A sees B's task first.
146	- **R-3.6** GIVEN no stored task, WHEN the list is opened, THEN the screen says the list is empty,
147	  with a sentence about what to do, and shows no error.
148	
149	### R-4: Marking a task done and not done — **P1**
150	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to tick a task done, and tick it back if I ticked it by
151	mistake, so that the list says what is left to do.
152	**Why this priority:** It is the point of the request: "mark that a task is done" (`request.md`).
153	**Independent test:** Tick one task done, reload, tick it back, reload.
154	
155	1. WHEN a person marks a not-done task as done, the system SHALL record it as done.
156	2. WHEN a person marks a done task as not done, the system SHALL record it as not done (`Q-2`).
157	3. WHEN a person marks a task, the system SHALL record the state the person chose, whatever
158	   state was stored at that moment: marking done a task already done leaves it done, and marking
159	   not done a task already not done leaves it not done.
160	4. WHEN a task is marked done or not done, the system SHALL leave its text unchanged.
161	5. The system SHALL show, for every task in the list, whether it is done, and SHALL show a done
162	   task differently from a not-done one (`Q-4`).
163	6. WHILE a task is shown as done, the system SHALL keep its text at or above the contrast floor
164	   every text on screen clears, 4.5:1 against the surface it is painted on
165	   (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens).
166	
167	**Acceptance**
168	- **R-4.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN a person marks it done and reloads the
169	  list, THEN "Buy bread" is shown as done, with the same text, in the same position.
170	- **R-4.2** GIVEN the done task "Buy bread", WHEN a person marks it not done and reloads the list,
171	  THEN it is shown as not done.
172	- **R-4.3** GIVEN "Buy bread" is already done, because another person marked it, while this
173	  person's screen still shows it not done, WHEN this person marks it done, THEN it stays done and
174	  is not switched back to not done.
175	- **R-4.4** GIVEN a list holding one done task and one not-done task, WHEN it is shown, THEN the
176	  two are shown differently, and the done task's text measures at least 4.5:1 against the surface
177	  behind it.
178	
179	### R-5: Two screens and the way between them — **P1**
180	**Objective:** As somebody using the application, I want to move between the guestbook and the
181	to-do list, so that I can find the list without knowing its address while the guestbook stays
182	where it was.
183	**Why this priority:** A to-do list at an address nobody is shown is a list nobody uses.
184	`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column says a second screen "must add navigation here".
185	**Independent test:** From the guestbook, reach the to-do list and come back without typing an
186	address.
187	
188	1. The system SHALL give the to-do list an address of its own, and entering that address
189	   directly SHALL open the list (`Q-5`).
190	2. WHILE a person is on the guestbook screen or on the to-do list screen, the system SHALL offer
191	   a way to reach the other screen without typing an address (`Q-1`).
192	3. WHEN a person opens the application's main address, the system SHALL show the guestbook, as it
193	   does today (`Q-5`).
194	4. The system SHALL NOT say anywhere on its screens that the application has one screen (`Q-1`:
195	   that copy "stops being true").
196	
197	**Acceptance**
198	- **R-5.1** GIVEN the to-do list's own address, WHEN a person enters it in the browser, THEN the
199	  to-do list opens.
200	- **R-5.2** GIVEN the guestbook screen, WHEN a person uses the way to the other screen, THEN the
201	  to-do list opens with no address typed. GIVEN the to-do list screen, the same way leads back
202	  to the guestbook.
203	- **R-5.3** GIVEN the application's main address, WHEN it is opened, THEN the guestbook is shown.
204	- **R-5.4** GIVEN an address the application does not know, WHEN it is opened, THEN the page that
205	  says nothing is there does not claim the application has one screen.
206	
207	### R-6: Editing a task's text — **P2**
208	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to correct a task's text, so that a typo or a changed plan does
209	not mean deleting the task and adding it again.
210	**Why this priority:** The list works without it, because delete and re-add is a workaround, but
211	the user put it in scope (`Q-3`).
212	**Independent test:** Edit one task's text and read it back.
213	
214	1. WHEN a person changes a task's text, the system SHALL store the new text and show it in the
215	   task's place.
216	2. WHEN a task's text is edited, the system SHALL leave the task's state as it is stored at that
217	   moment and leave its moment of adding unchanged (`Q-9`: "Editing changes the text only, never
218	   done or not done").
219	3. WHERE a task is done, the system SHALL let a person edit its text exactly as it does for a
220	   not-done task (`Q-9`).
221	4. IF an edited text is empty after trimming, is longer than 200 code points after normalizing
222	   and trimming, or, once trimmed, still carries a line break, THEN the system SHALL refuse the
223	   edit, keep the task's previous text, and tell the person why (`R-2`).
224	
225	**Acceptance**
226	- **R-6.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bred", WHEN it is edited to "Buy bread", THEN the list
227	  shows "Buy bread", not done, in the same position.
228	- **R-6.2** GIVEN the done task "Call the plumber", WHEN it is edited to "Call the plumber again",
229	  THEN it is still done and in the same position.
230	- **R-6.3** GIVEN the task "Buy bread", WHEN it is edited to "   ", THEN the edit is refused and the
231	  task still reads "Buy bread". An edit to a text of 201 code points is refused the same way. An
232	  edit to a text with a line break between two words is refused the same way.
233	
234	### R-7: Deleting a task — **P2**
235	**Objective:** As anybody, I want to remove a task, with one question before it goes, so that a
236	list does not fill with things nobody will do and a slip of the mouse deletes nothing.
237	**Why this priority:** Useful and independent of every other operation, and in scope (`Q-3`).
238	**Independent test:** Delete one task out of three and confirm the other two remain.
239	
240	1. WHEN a person asks to delete a task, the system SHALL ask them to confirm before it deletes
241	   anything (`Q-9`).
242	2. WHEN the person confirms, the system SHALL delete the task permanently, with no bin, no undo
243	   and no recovery (`Q-9`).
244	3. IF the person does not confirm, THEN the system SHALL leave the task as it was.
245	4. WHEN a task is deleted, the system SHALL leave every other task unchanged.
246	
247	**Acceptance**
248	- **R-7.1** GIVEN the tasks "Alpha", "Beta" and "Gamma", WHEN a person deletes "Beta" and
249	  confirms, THEN the list holds "Alpha" and "Gamma", and "Beta" does not come back after a reload.
250	- **R-7.2** GIVEN the task "Beta", WHEN a person asks to delete it and then cancels, THEN "Beta"
251	  is still on the list, unchanged.
252	
253	### R-8: A task that no longer exists — **P2**
254	**Objective:** As somebody whose screen is out of date, I want to be told clearly when the task I
255	am acting on has been deleted, so that I never believe I changed something that is gone.
256	**Why this priority:** Without identity anybody can delete any task, so this happens as soon as
257	two people use the list. The user asked for "a clear message" (`Q-9`).
258	**Independent test:** Delete a task through one browser, then try to mark it done through
259	another.
260	
261	1. IF a person edits, marks or deletes a task that has already been deleted, THEN the system
262	   SHALL change nothing, create no task, and tell the person the task no longer exists.
263	2. IF the same task is deleted a second time, THEN the system SHALL refuse and tell the person it
264	   no longer exists, rather than report a deletion it did not perform.
265	
266	**Acceptance**
267	- **R-8.1** GIVEN person A's screen shows "Buy bread" and person B has deleted it, WHEN A marks it
268	  done, THEN A is told the task no longer exists, and after a reload no "Buy bread" is on the list.
269	- **R-8.2** GIVEN the same situation, WHEN A saves an edit of "Buy bread" to "Buy rye bread", THEN
270	  A is told the task no longer exists, and no task "Buy rye bread" appears.
271	- **R-8.3** GIVEN a task already deleted, WHEN it is deleted again, THEN the person is told it no
272	  longer exists.
273	
274	### R-9: Two people changing one task at once — **P2**
275	**Objective:** As one of several people sharing the list, I want changes made at the same moment
276	to settle predictably, so that my tick is never silently undone by somebody else's edit.
277	**Why this priority:** It applies only when two people act on one task at once, but when that
278	happens and this requirement is missing, a change is lost with nothing on screen to show it.
279	**Independent test:** Send an edit and a mark for one task before either one is answered.
280	
281	1. WHEN two people change the text of the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL keep
282	   the text from the change applied later (`Q-9`: "the later change wins").
283	2. WHEN one person edits a task's text while another marks the same task at the same moment, the
284	   system SHALL keep both changes, the edited text and the chosen state, in whichever order they
285	   are applied.
286	3. WHEN two people mark the same task at the same moment, the system SHALL end with the state
287	   chosen in the change applied later.
288	
289	"At the same moment" means that both changes are sent before either one is answered.
290	
291	**Acceptance**
292	- **R-9.1** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B marks it
293	  done, both before either is answered, THEN the task reads "Buy rye bread" and is done, whichever
294	  change was applied first.
295	- **R-9.2** GIVEN the task "Buy bread", WHEN A edits it to "Buy rye bread" and B edits it to "Buy
296	  white bread", and B's change is applied later, THEN the task reads "Buy white bread".
297	- **R-9.3** GIVEN the not-done task "Buy bread", WHEN A and B both mark it done, both before either
298	  is answered, THEN it is done.
299	
300	### R-10: A change that did not go through is not shown as made — **P2**
301	**Objective:** As somebody on a poor connection, I want to know when my change did not go
302	through, so that I never believe a task was added, ticked, edited or deleted when it was not.
303	**Why this priority:** The list belongs to the application, not to the browser (`brainstorm.md`
304	§ What was settled). A screen showing a change the application never stored lies about the one
305	thing the list is for.
306	**Independent test:** Cut the service off, tick a task, and read the screen.
307	
308	1. IF adding, marking, editing or deleting a task is not stored, because the service cannot be
309	   reached or refuses the change, THEN the system SHALL tell the person the change was not made.
310	2. IF a change was not stored, THEN the system SHALL NOT show it in the list as made.
311	3. IF the list cannot be read, THEN the system SHALL say that the list failed to load and SHALL NOT
312	   say that the list is empty.
313	
314	**Acceptance**
315	- **R-10.1** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person marks "Buy bread" done, THEN the
316	  screen says the change was not made and "Buy bread" is shown as not done.
317	- **R-10.2** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN a person adds a task, THEN the screen says
318	  the task was not added and no new task appears in the list.
319	- **R-10.3** GIVEN the service cannot be reached, WHEN the to-do list is opened, THEN the screen
320	  says the list failed to load, and does not show the empty-list sentence of `R-3.6`.
321	
322	### R-11: Example tasks in a new environment — **P3**
323	**Objective:** As a reviewer opening a freshly created environment, I want a few example tasks
324	already on the list, so that I can judge the screen without typing.
325	**Why this priority:** The list works without it. A preview with an empty list gives nobody
326	anything to judge (`Q-8`).
327	**Independent test:** Bring up a freshly created environment and open the to-do list.
328	**Verified-by:** manual — the seeder is proved by `tests/tooling/` and the seed corpus by `tests/fitness/`, neither of which carries a requirement citation by rule (`spec/design/testing.md` § The UI smoke is not a traceability surface), and the black box starts the application with `--no-seed`; a person opens a freshly created environment and counts the example tasks.
329	
330	1. WHEN an environment whose to-do list holds no task is filled with example data, whatever the
331	   guestbook holds, the system SHALL put at least three example tasks on the to-do list (`Q-10`:
332	   "Yes, each list is filled on its own").
333	2. The system SHALL hold every example task to the text rules of `R-2`, and SHALL keep every
334	   example task under 150 code points (the seed corpus is looked at, not a boundary file).
335	3. IF the environment is production, THEN the system SHALL add no example task
336	   (`spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new environment starts with).
337	4. IF the to-do list already holds at least one task, THEN the system SHALL add no example task,
338	   so that filling an environment again never duplicates them.
339	5. WHEN an environment is filled with example data, the system SHALL decide whether to give the
340	   guestbook its welcome entries by what the guestbook holds alone, whatever the to-do list holds
341	   (`Q-10`).
342	6. WHEN the example tasks have been put on the to-do list, the system SHALL mark at least one of
343	   them done (`Q-12`: "Yes, at least one is done"). It is added not done and then marked, because
344	   a new task is never born done (`R-1` clause 3).
345	
346	**Acceptance**
347	- **R-11.1** GIVEN a freshly created environment, WHEN it has been filled with example data, THEN
348	  the to-do list shows at least three tasks.
349	- **R-11.2** GIVEN an environment whose to-do list holds one task, WHEN it is filled with example
350	  data again, THEN the list still holds exactly that one task.
351	- **R-11.3** GIVEN a production environment, WHEN filling it with example data is attempted, THEN
352	  no task is added.
353	- **R-11.4** GIVEN the example tasks, WHEN each is measured by the rules of `R-2`, THEN each is
354	  accepted and none reaches 150 code points.
355	- **R-11.5** GIVEN an environment whose guestbook holds its welcome entries and whose to-do list is
356	  empty, WHEN it is filled, THEN the list shows the example tasks and the guestbook holds exactly
357	  the entries it held before.
358	- **R-11.6** GIVEN a to-do list holding one task and an empty guestbook, WHEN it is filled, THEN
359	  the guestbook gets its welcome entries and the list still holds exactly that one task.
360	- **R-11.7** GIVEN a to-do list just filled with example tasks, WHEN it is shown, THEN at least one
361	  example task is shown as done.

471	### Races
472	- **W-1: an edit against a mark on one task.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the stored
473	  task (text and state), replaces the text and writes the whole task back. Between that read and
474	  that write the mark has stored "done". What the database holds at that moment is "done", and
475	  the edit's write-back replaces it with the "not done" it read. `R-9` clause 2 and `R-6`
476	  clause 2 forbid that outcome. The only update path in the codebase today overwrites with no
477	  version check (`impact.md`, `app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py:206`), so
478	  nothing in the store holds this rule yet (constitution, article VI). Only a concurrent test can
479	  tell the two apart (`spec/design/testing.md` § Choosing what proves what).
480	- **W-2: two marks from screens that are out of date.** The read-then-write happens if a mark is
481	  built as "read the state, store its opposite". A reads not done and stores done. B, who saw not
482	  done on the screen, reads done and stores not done. The database ends "not done", although both
483	  people chose done. `R-4` clause 3 (record the chosen state) removes the read.
484	- **W-3: an edit or a mark against a delete.** The read-then-write: the edit reads the task (it
485	  exists), the delete removes it, then the edit writes. What the database holds at that moment is
486	  no task. A write that creates on absence brings the task back. `R-8` clause 1 ("create no task")
487	  forbids it.
488	- **W-4: two adds in the same instant.** There is no read. Both tasks are stored with the same
489	  moment of adding, and only a tie-break makes the order total (`R-3` clause 3).
490	- **W-5: filling a new environment against a person adding.** The read-then-write: filling reads
491	  "the to-do list is empty", a person adds a task, then filling posts the example tasks. The
492	  database ends with the person's task plus the examples. No constraint stands behind the check.
493	  The guestbook's filling has the same exposure today. It is rare, because it needs a person to
494	  add a task in the seconds between that read and those posts, during a deploy to an environment
495	  whose to-do list is empty (`R-11` clause 1, `Q-10`).
496	- **W-6: two fillings of one environment.** Deploy and preview both run on one environment.
497	  Both read "empty" and both post, so the examples appear twice. This is rare, and the guestbook
498	  has the same exposure today.
499	
500	### With no defined behaviour
501	- When a person presses "add" a second time before the first add is answered, does the second
502	  press add a second task, or is it held off until the first is answered?
503	- After an add fails, does the field keep what was typed? After an add succeeds, is the field
504	  emptied?
505	- What does the screen show while a write waits 30 s for its answer, and can the person act on
506	  other tasks meanwhile?
507	- Is there a largest number of tasks the list holds or shows? With no pages (`Q-9`), every task
508	  is read at once, and nothing bounds how many there are.
509	- After "the task no longer exists" (`R-8`), does the list drop that task at once or on the next
510	  reload?

649	## Non-Goals
650	- **Removing or changing the guestbook.** The user chose to keep it beside the list (`Q-1`), and
651	  every guestbook behaviour and suite stays as it is (`SC-5`).
652	- **A Polish screen or any translation.** The screen is English, like the rest (`Q-7`,
653	  `spec/design/conventions.md` § Language).
654	- **Search, pages, filters (for example "only open tasks") and a "clear all done" action.**
655	  Everything is on one list (`Q-9`). `BR-05` stays the guestbook's.
656	- **Due dates, priorities, assigned people, categories and more than one list.** It is one shared
657	  list of one-line tasks (`Q-9`).
658	- **Live updates.** Other people's changes appear when the list is reloaded (`Q-9`, `R-3`
659	  clause 5). Nothing pushes them to an open screen.
660	- **Accounts, sign-in, "my tasks", and recording who added or ticked a task.** This is the
661	  standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals): anybody adds, marks, edits and
662	  deletes any task.
663	- **Moderation.** The same standing non-goal: no reports, no hiding.
664	- **Warning a person that somebody else's change overwrote theirs.** "The later change wins"
665	  (`Q-9`), and nobody is told their change was replaced (`R-9`).
666	- **A bin, undo, or restoring a deleted task.** "Gone for good" (`Q-9`, `R-7` clause 2).
667	- **Moving done tasks to the bottom or into a separate section.** Ticking never moves a task
668	  (`Q-4`, `R-3` clause 4).
669	- **Reordering tasks by hand.** The order is the moment of adding, newest first (`Q-6`), and
670	  nothing else sets it.
671	- **A mobile design of the new screen.** This is the standing non-goal (`spec/invariants.md`
672	  § Deliberate non-goals, "A mobile version").
673	- **A retention policy for tasks.** A task lives until somebody deletes it, as an entry does
674	  under the standing non-goal. For tasks this is assumed, not decided (`A-2`, § Named
675	  assumptions).
676	- **Detecting a duplicate caused by a retried add.** The same text twice is two tasks by
677	  decision (`Q-9`, `R-1` clause 5), so `E-20` leaves a duplicate for a person to delete.
678	
679	## Bounds
680	
681	| Quantity | Value | Where it comes from |
682	|---|---|---|
683	| Task text, maximum | 200 code points, after NFC normalization and trimming | `Q-9` ("up to 200 characters"). The unit is the one every text field is measured in (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Backend on `text.py`; `spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters) |
684	| Task text, minimum | 1 code point after trimming | `Q-9` ("An empty task, or one made only of spaces, is refused") |
685	| Trim set | the written 30-code-point set | `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`, `app/platform/schemas/text.py` |
686	| Line break inside a task | refused; the set is U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 | `Q-11` for the refusal; the set is assumption `A-1` (§ Named assumptions) |
687	| Emoji boundary value | 200 × U+1F600 = 200 code points = 400 UTF-16 code units; 201 refused | `R-2.3`, from the `D-04` incident |
688	| Decomposed boundary value | 200 × (U+0065 U+0301) = 400 code points before NFC, 200 after | `R-2.4`, from `BR-01`'s normalization |
689	| Padding boundary value | 2 + 200 + 2 = 204 as typed, accepted; 205 spaces, refused as empty | `R-2.5`, from the `api.md` trim-order incident |
690	| Tasks shown per read | all of them, with no pages | `Q-9` |
691	| List size that proves "no pages" | 101 tasks | one more than 100, the guestbook's largest piece (`spec/design/api.md` § Collection read parameters), and more than its default of 20 |
692	| Example tasks, minimum | 3 | `Q-8` ("a few"), with the seed-half rule that a list is at least three items (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_the_seed_half_shows_a_list_rather_than_an_entry`) |
693	| Example tasks done, minimum | 1 | `Q-12` |
694	| Example task, maximum length | under 150 code points (0.75 × 200) | the seed-half margin in `tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py::test_no_seed_entry_stands_near_a_published_limit` |
695	| Contrast of a done task's text | at least 4.5:1 against the surface behind it | `spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens (WCAG 2.1, 1.4.3) |
696	| "At the same moment" | both changes sent before either is answered | `R-9` |
697	
698	The search phrase's bound is also 200 code points (`QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`). That is two rules
699	sharing a number, and a test that reads the phrase's constant to prove the task's bound proves
700	the wrong rule.
701	
702	## Open questions
703	- **`D1`: answered.** `Q-10` → A, each list is filled on its own (`R-11` clause 1).
704	- **`D2`: answered.** `Q-11` → A, refuse it with its own message (`R-2` clause 6).
705	- **`D3`: answered.** `Q-12` → A, at least one example is done (`R-11` clause 6).
706	- **Double add while the first is in flight, what the field holds after an add, the screen while
707	  a write waits, the list after "no longer exists", and a largest number of tasks.** None of
708	  these blocks the requirements. They are for the design stage: the screen specification and the
709	  mock-up the user approves. A product rule the design needs from them goes back to the user,
710	  not into a design document.
711	- **The frame's words with two screens: the lockup name, the footer about "entries", the header
712	  fact, and where the not-found page leads.** These block nothing here. `brainstorm.md` § Open
713	  gives them to the mock-up, for the user to approve there. `R-5` clause 4 is the only
714	  constraint on them in this document.
715	
716	## Named assumptions
717	
718	*This stage's question budget is spent: `sdd-engine loop ask --raise` refused a thirteenth
719	question. What no answer decides is written here as an assumption, in the form "Assumed: …, say
720	so if not". No item below is a human decision yet. The user confirms or overrules each one
721	at the approval of this document, which ends the stage.*
722	
723	- **`A-1`: which characters are a line break (`R-2` clause 6, `R-6` clause 4).** Assumed: a line
724	  break is any of U+000A (line feed), U+000B (line tabulation), U+000C (form feed), U+000D
725	  (carriage return), U+0085 (next line), U+2028 (line separator) and U+2029 (paragraph
726	  separator): one written set that the screen and the service both read, so a pasted text is
727	  refused the same way on both sides. Say so if not. The other reading is U+000A and U+000D
728	  alone, which keeps the other five as content inside a task, the way a guestbook signature keeps
729	  U+0085 (`text-measurement.json` case `next_line_inside_is_kept`). The set is written down
730	  because the two languages' own line-break defaults disagree, among others about U+000B, U+000C
731	  and U+0085 (COH-requirements-4 in `review/coherence.md`), and `R-2` clause 5 fails if each side
732	  takes its own. **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
733	- **`A-2`: a task lives until somebody deletes it (§ Non-Goals).** Assumed: nothing removes a
734	  task except a person deleting it, with no expiry and no retention policy, as for a guestbook
735	  entry (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals, "A data retention policy"). Say so if not.
736	  `Q-9` settled that anybody may delete any task and that a deleted task is gone for good. It did
737	  not settle whether a task can go without anybody deleting it. Until this is confirmed, that
738	  non-goal keeps its wording for entries alone. **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
739	- **`A-3`: where the inside of a task's text ends (`R-2` clauses 4 and 6, `R-6` clause 4).**
740	  Assumed: the line-break rule reads the text as `R-2` clause 1 has trimmed it, so a line break
741	  the trim leaves in the text is refused wherever it sits. A character that shows nothing but is
742	  not in the trim set, such as U+200B (zero width space) or U+180E (Mongolian vowel separator), is
743	  content: "Buy bread", a line feed, then U+200B is refused, because clause 1 removes neither the
744	  U+200B nor the line feed before it. Say so if not. The other reading is "between the first and
745	  last visible character", the phrase the first draft used as a gloss on "inside": it lets that
746	  line feed through and stores it, and it needs a written definition of "visible" that the screen
747	  and the service both read, which no document has. The trim reading is the one `scenarios.md`
748	  S-9 already holds ("the line break rule runs before trimming" fails it) and the one
749	  `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01` uses for entries ("Whitespace *inside* a value is
750	  content and is kept; only the ends go") (COH-requirements-8 in `review/coherence.md`).
751	  **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
752	- **`A-4`: what "the guestbook suites run unchanged" promises (`SC-5`).** Assumed: the 22
753	  scenarios of `e2e/suite/features/guestbook.feature` run unedited, and the UI smoke's guestbook
754	  tests keep asserting what they assert today, while a locator in `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py` that
755	  names the lockup or a navigation link may follow the names the user approves in the mock-up.
756	  Say so if not. The other reading keeps the smoke unedited too, and so decides in advance a copy
757	  question § Open questions gives to the mock-up: the lockup stays "Guestbook", and no navigation
758	  link takes that exact name. The smoke finds the lockup link by that exact name
759	  (`e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`:40, :93, :373; `frontend/src/components/shell/PageFrame.tsx`:24), so
760	  under that reading a renamed lockup, or a second link named "Guestbook", turns it red
761	  (COH-requirements-9 in `review/coherence.md`). **Status:** assumed, awaiting the user.
762	
763	## Self-check
764	
765	1. [Completeness] [§ R-1] Does the moment of adding need to be visible to anybody, or does it
766	   serve only the order? If a person has to see it, the screen needs a requirement and the
767	   mock-up a place for it. As written, it serves `R-3` alone.
768	2. [Coherence] [§ R-1] Is "a new task is recorded not done, whatever the request claims" a rule
769	   the user stated, or one inferred from "a to-do list"? If a reviewer calls it invented, it goes
770	   to the user. The rejected reading is that a client can add a task already done.
771	3. [Clarity] [§ R-2] Can a second implementer find "the written 30-code-point set" without
772	   reading guestbook code? It points at `BR-01` and `text.py`. If tasks land in another context,
773	   the set has to be shared rather than copied, or two copies drift.
774	4. [Completeness] [§ R-2] What happens to a line break inside a text? It is refused with a reason
775	   of its own (`Q-11`, `R-2` clause 6, `R-2.7`). Which characters are a line break is assumption
776	   `A-1`, for the user to confirm at this document's approval.
777	5. [Measurability] [§ R-2] Can "the screen takes every character" in `R-2.3` be observed in a
778	   suite that owns citations? It can over the rule the screen applies, in vitest. The typing and
779	   pasting half only the UI smoke sees, and the smoke owns no citation. If design finds no vitest
780	   seam, that half loses its automated proof.
781	6. [Compliance] [§ R-2] Does `tests/fitness/test_length_constants.py` hold the new 200 and its
782	   browser copy? No, it names three bounds. Unless it is extended, the new copy stands unheld, as
783	   the signature's unit did before `D-04`.
784	7. [Clarity] [§ R-3] Does "newest first" still mean "by moment of adding" after an edit? Yes, by
785	   clause 4. A reader who takes "newest" as "most recently changed" makes edited tasks jump, and
786	   `R-3.4` pins the intended reading.
787	8. [Completeness] [§ R-3] Is there a number of tasks beyond which "every task on one list" stops
788	   being acceptable? None is stated. If the design needs a ceiling, that is a product question for
789	   the user, not a design choice.
790	9. [Measurability] [§ R-3] Can `R-3.2` be observed without control of the clock? Only if a test
791	   can store two tasks with an equal moment of adding. Otherwise the tie-break passes by luck.
792	10. [Clarity] [§ R-4] Is "mark done" setting a chosen state, or flipping the stored one? It is
793	    written as setting (clause 3). A flip built by the design fails `R-4.3` and `R-9.3` under
794	    screens that are out of date.
795	11. [Coherence] [§ R-4] Does clause 6 restate a rule that already has a home
796	    (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § Tokens)? Yes, on purpose, as the observable form of the
797	    defect this screen invites. If the frame's floor moves, this clause follows it rather than
798	    competing with it.
799	12. [Measurability] [§ R-4] Can "shown differently" be judged without a person? Only through what
800	    a test can read, such as the done state as the page exposes it. The visual form belongs to the
801	    mock-up.
802	13. [Completeness] [§ R-5] Where does the not-found page lead when there are two screens? That is
803	    not stated. If it leads only to the guestbook, a visitor who wanted the to-do list is one step
804	    further away, which `R-5` does not forbid.
805	14. [Compliance] [§ R-5] Would a navigation link named exactly "Guestbook" break the exact lookups
806	    in `e2e/ui/test_smoke.py`? Yes: two links with one name. The design either names the link
807	    differently, or the smoke's locator changes in the same change.
808	15. [Coherence] [§ R-6] Does "leave the task's state as it is stored at that moment" contradict
809	    "the later change wins"? Only if "later wins" is read as applying to the whole task. It is
810	    read per aspect (text, state). If the user meant the whole task, `R-9` clause 2 is the
811	    sentence to take back to them.
812	16. [Completeness] [§ R-7] Does the confirmation have to name the task? That is not stated. The
813	    guestbook's dialog does name the entry (`spec/design/ui/guestbook.md` § The delete dialog), so
814	    the mock-up will likely copy it. It is not a requirement here.
815	17. [Clarity] [§ R-8] Does "tell the person the task no longer exists" require the list to drop
816	    that task at once? No, and it is open. If the design leaves it on screen, a second attempt
817	    meets the same message.
818	18. [Clarity] [§ R-9] Is "the change applied later" well defined when two requests overlap? It
819	    means the one whose write the store applied last. If a reviewer needs arrival order instead, a
820	    mechanism beyond the store's own ordering is needed.
821	19. [Measurability] [§ R-9] Can `R-9.1` be proved by a sequential test? No. An edit followed by a
822	    mark passes over a whole-task write-back too. Only concurrent requests tell the two apart
823	    (constitution, article VI).
824	20. [Completeness] [§ R-10] Is the typed text still in the field after a failed add? That is open.
825	    If it is not, the person retypes it, and nothing here says whether that is acceptable.
826	21. [Completeness] [§ R-11] What happens in an environment that existed before this change and
827	    whose to-do list is empty? That is `D1`, answered by `Q-10` → A (`R-11` clause 1). Option A
828	    turns `tests/tooling/test_seed_golden_set.py::test_a_guest_book_with_entries_is_left_alone`
829	    red.
830	22. [Compliance] [§ R-11] Is `**Verified-by:** manual` honest here, or does a citation-owning
831	    suite exist that proves it? `tests/tooling/` and `tests/fitness/` own no citation, and the black box runs
832	    with `--no-seed`. If design-testing finds a surface, the marker has to be removed, not left
833	    standing beside a test.
834	23. [Coherence] [Gap] Do the non-goals in `spec/invariants.md`, worded for entries, bind the to-do
835	    list? By intent yes, by wording no. Only the convergence round edits that file, so the finding
836	    goes there. It went there as COH-requirements-5: authentication now covers tasks, and
837	    retention waits on `A-2`.
838	24. [Compliance] [Gap] Which bounded context owns a task? That is not a requirement: it is
839	    design-domain's call. If tasks live inside the guestbook context, the closing sentence of
840	    `P-01` ("An entry either exists or it does not") stops describing that context.

# Requirements — the to-do list: add tasks and mark them done

**Change:** CR-2609-823a
**Source:** request.md, impact.md, brainstorm.md (answers `Q-1`…`Q-9`), and the answers
`Q-10`…`Q-12` recorded in the change record on 2026-09-24

## Goal

Anybody who opens the application can reach a second screen, a shared to-do list, add a task
of one line, tick it done and back, correct it and delete it, while the guestbook stays where
it is and keeps working as it does today.

Words used below, none of which is in `spec/glossary.md` yet (giving them a home is the design
stage's job): a **task** is one line of text somebody put on the list; **the to-do list** is the
one list of tasks every visitor shares; **done** and **not done** are the one state a task has,
switched both ways; **the moment of adding** is when the system stored a task. It orders the
list and never changes.

## Success criteria

| Id | Criterion | Baseline | How measured after delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SC-1** | A person who has never seen the to-do list reaches it from the guestbook, adds a task and finds it at the top of the list, with no instruction. | None. Nobody can add a task today: no to-do concept exists in the specification or in the code (`impact.md` § What is missing). | The requester follows the `uat.md` script on the delivered branch before merging and records pass or fail per step. That is the one look after delivery this template schedules. |
| **SC-2** | Two people looking at the list after a reload see the same tasks, in the same order, with the same done marks. | None. The guestbook is the only thing people share today, and it has no state anybody marks. | The requester checks it at UAT with two browser windows (`uat.md`). The scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-3` and `CR-2609-823a/R-9` re-check it on every CI run of the branch. |
| **SC-3** | A task ticked done by mistake goes back to not done in one action, and neither action moves it in the list. | None. Nothing the application stores has a state that can be switched (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`: "An entry either exists or it does not"). | A `uat.md` step at UAT, plus the scenarios tagged `CR-2609-823a/R-4` on every CI run. |
| **SC-4** | A reviewer who opens a freshly created environment sees example tasks on the list without typing any. | A freshly created environment opens today with the guestbook's welcome entries (`golden-set/seed/entries-welcome.json`) and nothing else. | The reviewer opens the first preview of this branch (Actions → Preview), or runs `./scripts/start.sh` on a fresh clone, and counts the example tasks. This is manual because the black box starts with `--no-seed` (`R-11`). |
